name: 3d-scene-schema
summary: Engine-independent description of scenes, objects, and components.
purpose: Defines one shared, serializable scene structure so that content authored once can be loaded by any engine integration and read by constructors, tools, and agents.
usage: Constructors and game packages describe their worlds with this schema. Engine integrations such as 3d-unity-scene read it and build the matching scene at runtime.
examples: A level described as data and loaded by Unity
A constructor generating a starter scene for a new game

name: 3d-unity-core
summary: Shared Unity foundation used by every other 3d-unity package.
purpose: Provides the small, product-independent base that the rest of the Unity packages build on, so each package stays focused on one responsibility.
install: https://github.com/itkamianets/3d-unity-core.git (Unity Package Manager, Add package from git URL)
usage: Add it first. Every other 3d-unity package declares it as a dependency, so installing any of them pulls it in automatically.
examples: Used as the dependency root of all 3d-unity packages

name: 3d-unity-scene
summary: Scene handling for Unity, driven by the shared scene schema.
purpose: Builds and manages Unity scenes from the engine-independent structures defined in 3d-scene-schema.
install: https://github.com/itkamianets/3d-unity-scene.git (Unity Package Manager, Add package from git URL)
usage: Point it at a scene description and it creates the matching objects and components. Constructors use it to assemble starter scenes.
features: Scene loading from the shared schema
examples: Loading a generated starter scene for a top-down game

name: 3d-unity-assets
summary: Asset loading and organization for Unity projects.
purpose: Gives constructors and games one consistent way to reference, load, and organize models, textures, audio, and other assets.
install: https://github.com/itkamianets/3d-unity-assets.git (Unity Package Manager, Add package from git URL)
usage: Scene descriptions reference assets by key; this package resolves and loads them so game code never depends on file paths.
examples: Resolving the prefab for a unit defined in a scene description

name: 3d-unity-interaction
summary: Input and interaction building blocks for Unity.
purpose: Provides reusable interaction primitives such as selecting, activating, and moving things, so constructors can compose them into camera- and gameplay-specific controls.
install: https://github.com/itkamianets/3d-unity-interaction.git (Unity Package Manager, Add package from git URL)
usage: Constructors combine these primitives into the control scheme of a given camera style, for example click-to-move for isometric games.
examples: Direct movement in a top-down constructor

name: 3d-unity-xr
purpose: Brings VR and AR capabilities into the same package architecture, so a constructor can target XR without game code touching device specifics.
install: https://github.com/itkamianets/3d-unity-xr.git (Unity Package Manager, Add package from git URL)
usage: Add it to a project that targets headsets or AR devices; interaction primitives are adapted to XR input automatically.
examples: A character-view game playable in a headset

name: 3d-unity-spatial
summary: Spatial data and queries for Unity.
purpose: Handles spatial structures such as grids, regions, and positional queries that strategy, isometric, and open-world games all need.
install: https://github.com/itkamianets/3d-unity-spatial.git (Unity Package Manager, Add package from git URL)
usage: Used by constructors that need to reason about space, such as grid-based placement in god-camera games.
examples: Grid placement for a city builder
Region queries for a strategy game
